notes: Isobutylene + HBr gives tert-butyl bromide via the 3° cation. Mechanism, traps (anti-Markovnikov, dibromide, alcohol) and retro distractors are all correct.

Chemistry and mechanism are right (2° to 3° hydride shift gives 2-chloro-2-methylbutane). But McMurry reports a ~1:1 mixture with the unrearranged chloride, which is a trap here. Made the trap text say 'expected major product' and added a review note about the course convention.

3,3-dimethyl-1-butene with H3O+ does a methyl shift and gives 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol (the Klein/Wade textbook example). Mechanism proton sources (H3O+/H2O) are right. Traps and retro distractors (oxymercuration, hydroboration) really do fail.

Mercurinium drawn as a 3-membered ring with Hg+ carrying one OAc (the Klein depiction, formal charge right). Water opens it at the more substituted C, giving the Markovnikov alcohol with no rearrangement. Resolved and removed the review note.
Anti-Markovnikov 3,3-dimethylbutan-1-ol. Concerted 4-centre step, then HOO- attack, 1,2-shift with retention, and alkoxide release/protonation all fine. Traps are correct.
RDKit: product is (1R,2R) trans-2-methylcyclohexanol (racemic). The trap is (1R,2S) cis, a diastereomer (3D check confirms cis/trans). Regiochemistry and retention are right.
RDKit: product (S,S) trans-1,2-dibromocyclohexane, chiral and racemic. The trap is the cis meso diastereomer. Bromonium formation and backside opening arrows are correct.
RDKit plus a 3D face check: product (1S,2S) has OH on the 3° C trans to Br. The cis trap is the (1S,2R) diastereomer. The regiochemistry trap and the dibromide trap are right.

cis-2-butene gives the (R,S) meso cis-epoxide, and the trap is the chiral (R,R) trans diastereomer. The concerted butterfly arrows are a valid electron-bookkeeping version (pi to O, O-H electrons form the second C-O, carbonyl O takes H, O-O to C=O).

Product is meso cis-diol (R,S) and the trap is (S,S) trans, as they should be. The [3+2] key-step arrows give a correct Os(VI) osmate ester. Fixed the hexanedial trap text (hot KMnO4 gives the diacid, not the dialdehyde) and removed the review note.
Product (S,S) trans-diol, racemic; the trap is the meso cis diol. The mechanism (epoxidation, protonation, backside water attack, deprotonation) is correct, and the retro distractors fail.
1-methylcyclopentene gives 5-oxohexanal with reductive (DMS) workup. The molozonide key-step arrows are correct. The oxidative-workup and KMnO4 retro distractors give 5-oxohexanoic acid.

Product is meso cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane and the trap is the chiral trans isomer. Changed reagentDisplay from H2, Pd/C to H2, Pt, because Pd is known to isomerize this tetrasubstituted alkene and give a lot of the trans product; the textbook syn example uses Pt/PtO2. The Pd aliases are still accepted.
Radical chain: Br adds to the CH2 and gives the 3° radical, then 1-bromo-2-methylpropane. 'Only HBr' is a true statement. Traps are right.
All read statements are true, including the step-5 mercurinium/bromonium bridging wording. Each choice has exactly one correct option with accurate explanations. Removed the review note.
